# Glossary of Terms

# **Product Platform Terms**

| **Heading** | **Description** |
| ---| --- |
| **NonID Matching** | NonID is a process which allows the joining of 2 datasets, both of which contain PII, by means of identifying common PII columns and by rules-based processing to determine the best matches between the tables. |
| **Overlap** | Performs KANON, Non-ID Matching, and PBI reporting.<br>Requires connection and data share.<br>Creates link table with customer key matches.<br>Allows audience selections. |
| **ACE and 3-Way ACE** | Performs KANON, custom ID Matching, and detailed PBI report.<br>Matches on Strive data (via view).<br>No data share required.<br>Subscription-dependent.<br>Allows audience selections. |
| **Custom Project** | Performs KANON and Non-ID Matching.<br>Requires connection and a data share.<br>Allows multiple shared/own tables.<br>No audience selections. |
| **Shoprite Financial Inclusion** | Uses Shoprite data.<br>Requires subscription.<br>Matches on identity and retro date.<br>Outputs usable in SQL Pad and Jupyter.<br>Allows adding own datasets.<br>Can add own datasets later.<br>No report. |
| **DG Predictive Modelling** | USA-only.<br>Dollar General subscription.<br>Non-ID matching.<br>Own tables only, no shared.<br>Can add own datasets later.<br>No report. |
| **Shoprite Lookalike** | Advanced model using Shoprite data.<br>Includes deduplication, feature engineering (clustering, cosine similarity).<br>Shoprite uploads audiences to Meta.<br>Allows audience selections.<br>Includes rental pricing. |
| **BasketScore** | Uses Shoprite data.<br>Available to CPB/Shoprite users.<br>Identity + retro date match.<br>Outputs BasketScore.<br>Usable in SQL Pad and Jupyter.<br>No report. |
| **Rainmaker Attribution** | Used for campaigns with Shoprite Rainmaker.<br>Requires Rainmaker and client datasets.<br>Produces PowerBI attribution report. |
| **Project** | Main component enabling data exchange between buyer and seller. |
| **Strive** | South Africa tenant with 60M+ records.<br>Omnisient tenant.<br>Several Synapse Stored Procedures and Pipelines exist to build Strive Universe and subsequent views based on the Strive Universe. |

# **iURNs in the Omnisient Platform**
## **What is an iURN?**
An **iURN** (Internal Unique Reference Number) is a unique row-level identifier that we inject into a dataset _before_ PII data is hashed and uploaded. It is always added in the dataset.

The iURN is the **first layer of privacy-preserving transformation** applied to identity data before any data leaves a client’s environment (e.g. via Desktop Connect or Server Connect). It is owned and controlled by the data provider.
## **Purpose of iURNs in the Omnisient Platform**
### **1. Privacy-Preserving Identity Mapping**
iURNs allow data providers to securely tokenize their customer identifiers, which are then used to:
*   Enable record linkage across datasets from different parties.
*   Prevent the exposure or misuse of raw PII.
*   Ensure that only hashed, privacy-compliant values are uploaded to the platform.
### **2. Linkage Anchor in the Identity Fabric**
The iURN is used internally as the anchor identity across the platform. It enables:
*   Surrogate Key generation.
*   Anonymous joining of datasets.
*   Consistent identity resolution without exposing PII.

## **How iURNs Fit Into the Omnisient Data Flow**

| **Stage** | **Role of iURN** |
| ---| --- |
| **Data Preparation (Client-side)** | Client hashes PII using SHA-256, optionally with salt. |
| **Upload (Desktop/Server Connect)** | iURN values are uploaded—no raw PII. |
| **Surrogate Key Mapping** | Omnisient creates an SKey from this iURNs (see the Glossary of Terms for more information about this process) for use in cleanrooms and other areas on the platform. |
| **Data Join / Collaboration** | Datasets from multiple parties are joined on matching DW Keys or their mapped Surrogate Keys. |
| **Insights & Analytics** | Analysis is performed using the Surrogate Keys derived from iURNs. |
| **Activation & Attribution** | Audiences are built and measured using keys linked back to iURNs without revealing identity. |

**Key Characteristics**
*   **Non-reversible**: iURNs are the result of one-way hashing and cannot be decoded back to PII.
*   **Deterministic**: iURN will always be unique. It's an ID we attach to the raw data and encrypted data on a row level.
*   **Scoped per Client**: iURNs are generated and owned by the client; each party maintains their own mapping from PII to iURN.
## **Example**
Let’s say a data provider wants to tokenize emails:
1. Raw email: [jane.doe@example.com](mailto:jane.doe@example.com)
2. Apply hashing: SHA-256([jane.doe@example.com](mailto:jane.doe@example.com) + salt)
3. Resulting iURN:
4. a32f0a1c5e3d4b8b0f3e1c20c798d8e1aabb44bb...

This iURN is then uploaded via Server Connect and used by Omnisient to map to a Surrogate Key, e.g. SK98321.
## How It's Used in Our System
*   We inject an iURN into each row before hashing.
*   A local copy of the original (unhashed) dataset is saved in an `.intersect` file — a lightweight SQLite database — containing the iURNs with the raw data.
*   After a project is completed and selections are made, the selected iURNs can be exported and joined with the original local data for further analysis or activation.
## **Summary**
iURNs are:
*   The **foundation of identity privacy** in Omnisient.
*   Used **only within the client’s control** to tokenize PII.
*   The **linking layer** that enables data collaboration without identity leakage.
*   Essential for secure joining, audience building, and downstream activation.

They allow the platform to enable insights and attribution across datasets without ever seeing or storing actual identities.

### **Flow**
### **iURN → Surrogate Key (SK)**
This is the **standard flow** in Omnisient and the most privacy-preserving.

**PII (e.g., email)** → **iURN (hashed by client)** → **Uploaded to Omnisient** → **Mapped to Surrogate Key (SK)** → **Used in platform (cleanroom, analytics, activation)**

**Summary**:
*   iURN is created **first** by the data provider.
*   Surrogate Key is generated **after** ingest to enable matching and internal usage.

# Surrogate Keys (SKey)

| **Reviewer** | **Reviewed/Verified** | **Last Reviewed** |
| ---| ---| --- |
| ??? | ✅ / ❌ | \- |

**PII → iURN → SK**

**In the context of Omnisient, a Surrogate Key (SK) is a system-generated, privacy-preserving identifier used to replace personally identifiable information (PII) such as email addresses, phone numbers, or ID numbers. These keys enable secure and anonymous data collaboration between parties without exposing any raw PII.**
# Purpose of Surrogate Keys in Omnisient:
**1\. Privacy-Preserving Data Collaboration**
Surrogate Keys allow two or more parties (e.g. a bank and a retailer) to link data without ever exposing PII to each other or to Omnisient.
*   Original PII stays inside the data owner’s environment.
*   The PII is transformed into an iURN (identity Universal Resource Name) or token.
*   This token is mapped to a surrogate key (SK), which becomes the join key used inside the Omnisient platform.

**2\. Platform Linking Mechanism**
Once both parties upload their data (tokenized), the Omnisient Identity Fabric uses the SKs to establish entity-level joins:
*   SKs allow Omnisient to perform **audience overlaps, segmentation, attribution, or enrichment** without ever touching raw PII.
*   For example, if both a telco and a grocery store tokenize their customer base, Omnisient will use the SK to find common entities between the two without either party knowing who the actual person is.

**3\. Persistent, Pseudonymous Identifiers**
SKs are designed to be:
*   Unique per identity within a project
*   Consistent within the scope of collaboration
*   Non-reversible back to the original PII (only the data owner has the mapping)
This makes SKs ideal for:
*   Privacy-preserving joins
*   Audience building
*   Attribution modeling
*   Reporting and enrichment
*   Consent-aware collaboration
# Flow Summary for Surrogate Key Use
1. A data owner (such as a retailer or financial institution) tokenizes their PII to generate iURNs using Omnisient’s on-premise tools like Desktop Connect or Server Connect.
2. The iURNs are uploaded to the platform.
3. The platform maps these iURNs to internal Surrogate Keys. These are the only keys used for any matching, joining, or analytics.
4. When two parties have tokenized and onboarded their datasets, the platform performs an anonymous join using the Surrogate Keys.
5. Insights, audience creation, and attribution processes occur on these keys.
6. At no point is PII exposed to Omnisient or the other party.

# Example Use Case

| **Step** | **Action** |
| ---| --- |
| **Retailer A tokenizes customer emails → gets iURNs** | abc123, def456 |
| **iURNs mapped to SKs like SK001, SK002** | One-time mapping |
| **Bank B does the same → abc123 → SK001** | Common identity linked via SK |
| **Platform now knows both parties have SK001** | But neither party knows the identity |
| **Omnisient enables overlap, insights, or ad activation** | Without PII exposure |

**Surrogate Keys are a foundational element of Omnisient’s Identity Fabric. They underpin secure joins, privacy-safe insights, and compliant data activation across cleanrooms and marketing channels.**

### Flow
### **SK Only (Legacy or Internal Data)**
Used when identity is not required or for non-collaborative use cases.

**Internal Record ID or Random UUID** → **Used as Surrogate Key directly**
**Summary**:
*   No iURN involved.
*   Typically used when datasets are anonymized and isolated by design.

# PII Types

## Knowledge Base
📖 [Supported Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Types](https://help.omnisient.com/en/articles/13513032-supported-personally-identifiable-information-pii-types)
## Summary of Supported Fields

| PII Type | Display Name | What it’s for | Important things to note |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| `iAPI` | Anonymous PI | Used to hide source data that doesn’t need to be treated as regulated PII (according to POPIA, GDPR, and UAE data protection laws), but should still be hashed before upload for privacy or internal policy reasons. |  |
| `iCCARDFIRST6` | Credit Card First 6 Digits | Useful for identifying the issuing bank / card type without exposing the full card number. |  |
| `iCCARDLAST4` | Credit Card Last 4 Digits | Helps verify payments or reconcile transactions while keeping the full card number protected. |  |
| `iCARDNO` | Credit Card Number | A full payment card number used for secure matching or transaction linking when required. |  |
| `iDOB` | Date Of Birth | Used for identity matching, segmentation, or age-based insights where allowed. |  |
| `iEMAIL` | Email Address | Supports person-level matching across datasets using a commonly available identifier. | Must follow standard email formats (e.g., `name@domain.com`). |
| `iFNAME` | First Name | Helps support name-based matching for use cases where names are needed (often alongside surname). |  |
| `iMEDAIDNO` | Medical Aid No | Used for healthcare / insurance matching and analysis while protecting member identity. |  |
| `iMERCHANTID` | Merchant ID | Enables secure transaction analysis and matching for retailers, payment providers, and financial institutions. |  |
| `iPASSPORTNO` | Passport Number | Used when matching individuals who do not have a national ID in the dataset. |  |
| `iPAYMENTACCREF` | Payment Account Reference | Allows tokenized tracking of payment accounts (e.g., customer account references) across datasets. |  |
| `iPHONE` | Phone No | Common identifier for matching customer records when email/ID is unavailable. |  |
| `iSNAME` | Last Name | Used for name-based matching and identity resolution when combined with other signals. | More effective when combined with first name and DOB/ID• Surnames alone are not unique. |
| `VIN` | Vehicle Identification Number | Identifies a specific vehicle using a globally standardized identifier. |  |

### South Africa Only

| PII Type | Display Name | What it’s for | Important things to note |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| `iADDITIONALID` | Additional ID Number | Supports clients who need to upload multiple ID columns in a single dataset (e.g., dependents, spouses, multiple household members). | Designed for “extra” ID fields beyond the primary ID number.<br><br>All values must be valid South African ID formats. |
| `iIDNO` | ID Number | Primary national ID field for strong, high-confidence person matching. | Only one ID Number field can be selected per dataset.<br><br>Must be a valid South African ID format. |
| `iSACOMPANYREGONO` | SA Company Business Registration Number | Improves local compliance and supports matching and configuration for South African businesses. |  |

### United States Only

| PII Type | Display Name | What it’s for | Important things to note |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| `iSSN` | Social Security Number | Strong identity field used in regions where SSNs are standard identifiers. |  |

# PII Validation & Standerdization

This document provides detailed information about how each type of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is validated and standardized in the Omnisient Validation SDK.

This document explains how each type of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is standardized and validated in the Omnisient Validation SDK.
## Email Address
**Validator:** `EmailAddressValidator`
### Standardization
*   Trim whitespace
*   Remove:
    *   Parentheses `(` `)`
    *   Spaces
    *   `mailto:` prefix
*   Convert to **lowercase**
### Validation Rules
*   Must match email regex
*   No consecutive dots (`..`)
*   Valid domain with ≥ 2-character TLD
### Examples

| Input | Standardized Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `User@Test.COM` | `user@test.com` | ✅ |
| `mailto:user@test.co.za` | `user@test.co.za` | ✅ |
| `user..test@domain.com` | unchanged | ❌ |

> ℹ️ **If validation fails, the original value is returned.**
### Error Message
*   `EMAIL Format Invalid`

* * *
## South African ID Number
**Validator:** `IDNumberValidator`
### Standardization
*   Trim whitespace
*   Remove spaces
*   Convert to **uppercase**
### Validation Rules
*   Exactly **13 digits**
*   Numeric only
*   Valid date (`YYMMDD`)
*   Valid **Luhn checksum**
*   Century inferred automatically
### Structure
`YYMMDD SSSS C A Z`

| Section | Meaning |
| ---| --- |
| YYMMDD | Date of birth |
| SSSS | Gender sequence |
| C | Citizenship |
| Z | Check digit |

### Examples

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `940427 6734 014` | `9404276734014` | ✅ |
| `8103121234033` | unchanged | ❌ |

### Error Messages
*   `IDNO Format Invalid [Length]`
*   `IDNO Invalid Character Found`
*   `IDNO Validation Failed`
*   `IDNO Invalid Checksum`

* * *
## Phone Number
**Validator:** `PhoneNumberValidator`
### Standardization
*   Trim whitespace
*   Parsed using **libphonenumber-csharp**
*   Returned as:
    *   National format (leading `0`)
    *   Country code
### Validation Rules
*   No letters
*   No `/ . , _`
*   Must be valid per libphonenumber
*   Uses `DefaultCountryCode` (default: ZA)
### Examples

| Input | Output | Country | Valid |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| `+27 (0) 83 487 9823` | `0834879823` | 27 | ✅ |
| `1234567890` | unchanged | — | ❌ |

### Error Message
*   `PHONE NO Invalid Format`

* * *
## Credit Card Number
**Validator:** `CreditCardNumberValidator`
### Standardization
*   Trim whitespace
*   Remove **all non-alphanumeric characters**
### Validation Rules
*   13–16 digits
*   Numeric only
*   Passes **Luhn check**
*   Recognized card brand
### Examples

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `4532-0151-1283-0366` | `4532015112830366` | ✅ |
| `1234567890123456` | unchanged | ❌ |

### Error Messages
*   Invalid characters
*   Invalid length
*   Failed checksum
*   Unknown card brand

* * *
## Credit Card – First 6 Digits (BIN)
**Validator:** `CreditCardNumberFirst6DigitsValidator`
### Rules
*   Exactly **6 digits**
*   Numeric only

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `453201` | `453201` | ✅ |
| `45320` | unchanged | ❌ |

* * *
## Credit Card – Last 4 Digits
**Validator:** `CreditCardNumberLast4DigitsValidator`
### Rules
*   Exactly **4 digits**
*   Numeric only

* * *
## Social Security Number (US)
**Validator:** `SSNValidator`
### Structure
`AAA-GG-SSSS`
### Invalid Conditions
*   Area: `000`, `666`, `900–999`
*   Group: `00`
*   Serial: `0000`
### Example

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `123-45-6789` | `123456789` | ✅ |

* * *
## SA Company Registration Number
**Validator:** `SACompanyRegNoValidator`
### Supported Formats
*   **Modern:** `YYYY/NNNNNN/NN`
*   **Old:** `XYYYY/NNNNNN`
### Examples

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `2004/123456/23` | `200412345623` | ✅ |
| `2050/123456/23` | unchanged | ❌ |

* * *
## VIN (Vehicle Identification Number)
**Validator:** `VINValidator`
### Rules
*   Exactly **17 characters**
*   Excludes `I`, `O`, `Q`
*   Must pass checksum

* * *
## Passport Number
**Validator:** `PassportNumberValidator`
*   No strict validation
*   Accepts any alphanumeric value after cleanup

* * *
## Date
**Validator:** `DateValidator`
### Output Format
`YYYYMMDD`
### Accepted Inputs
*   `YYYY-MM-DD`
*   `MM/DD/YYYY`
*   `DD/MM/YYYY`
*   Any .NET-parsable date

* * *
## Name
**Validator:** `NameValidator`
### Rules
*   Unicode letters only
*   Allows spaces, hyphens, apostrophes
*   Converted to **Title Case**

| Input | Output | Valid |
| ---| ---| --- |
| `john doe` | `John Doe` | ✅ |
| `john123` | unchanged | ❌ |

* * *
## Detection Chain Order
### 🇿🇦 South Africa
1. Email
2. SA ID
3. Phone
4. Credit Card
5. SA Company Reg
### 🇺🇸 United States
1. Email
2. SSN
3. Phone
4. Credit Card
* * *
## Common Standardization Pattern

```css
[^a-zA-Z0-9]
```

Used to remove **all special characters**.

* * *
## Error Handling Rules
✔ Return standardized value if valid
✔ Return original value if invalid
✔ Always set meaningful error messages

* * *
## Summary Table

| PII Type | Length | Case | Validation |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| Email | Variable | Lower | Regex |
| SA ID | 13 | Upper | Date + Luhn |
| Phone | Variable | — | libphonenumber |
| Credit Card | 13–16 | — | Luhn + Brand |
| SSN | 9 | — | Structural rules |
| VIN | 17 | Upper | Checksum |
| Name | Variable | Title | Unicode regex |

* * *
## 📦 Version Info
*   **SDK:** 1.0
*   **Frameworks:** .NET Standard 2.0, .NET 8
*   **Maintained by:** Omnisient Dev Team

# PII Detection and Leak Detection Process

## Purpose
This document describes how the platform detects Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and prevents PII leakage during data onboarding, ingestion, and downstream processing.
The process is designed to:
*   Detect PII as early as possible
*   Identify unexpected PII in non-PII fields
*   Quarantine risky datasets
*   Require explicit human approval before data is made usable
*   Prevent accidental exposure in the data warehouse
## Scope
This process applies to:
*   All datasets onboarded via Desktop Connect
*   All datasets onboarded via Server Connect
*   All data ingested into the Data Lake and Data Warehouse
## Supported PII Leak Types
PII leak detection is intentionally limited to fixed-domain identifiers:
*   ID Numbers
*   Social Security Numbers (SSN)
*   Email addresses
*   Phone numbers
## Process Overview
PII handling consists of three major stages:
1. PII field detection during onboarding
2. PII leak detection before and after upload
3. Quarantine, review, and approval before warehouse ingestion
## 1\. PII Field Detection (Pre-Upload)
### Desktop Connect
*   Uses column names
*   Uses a sample of data values
### Server Connect
*   Uses column names only
## 2\. PII Leak Detection – Desktop Connect (Pre-Upload)
*   Sample-based scan
*   Non-PII columns only
*   User must stop upload or mark false positive
## 3\. Full Dataset PII Leak Detection (Post-Upload)
*   Azure Function scans entire dataset
*   Known PII columns excluded
## 4\. Quarantine and Enforcement
*   Dataset quarantined if any leak detected
*   Blocked from data warehouse ingestion
*   Flagged in frontend and back office
## 5\. Back Office Review and Escalation
*   Back office notified via email
*   Can unflag, delete, or escalate to client
## 6\. Final Gate: Data Warehouse Ingestion
*   Only after all leaks unflagged
*   Then data is ingested and usable

# Overview
A project is a collection of components vital for data analysis and visualization within a container on our web application. It comprises of data tables, reports, and data extracts, known as selections. 

Project users have the convenience of accessing and collaborating on shared data by either opening the project in SQLPad or Jupyter Notebook, both seamlessly integrated into our web application.

# Shoprite Financial Inclusion

| **Reviewer** | **Reviewed/Verified** | **Last Reviewed** |
| ---| ---| --- |
| ??? | ✅ / ❌ | \- |

**Overview:**

This project enables a Tier 1 banks to use anonymized shopping data from a large retailer to assess the creditworthiness of people with no formal credit history. By securely matching shopping patterns with bank data, without sharing personal information, we help identify behaviors that predict creditworthiness. The goal is to use diverse, privacy-protected data sources, in this case retail data, to improve lending decisions and extend access to fair financial services. In this project template, the retailer’s customer data is matched to the bank’s records by both customer identity and a specific date, creating a clear, secure basis for analysis.

# Table of Contents
* * *
# Overview
Jupyter Notebook provides a flexible, code-based environment directly within our platform that enables users to perform **advanced analytics**, build models, and explore data in a secure and governed way.

Access is Jupyter Notebook is dependent on the company having a subscription.

* * *
# Platform Setup to Access Feature
*   The subscription "Jupyter" needs to be added for the company that wants use Jupyter Notebook. See how to access this feature in the Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15532](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15532)) documentation.

* * *
# How it Works
## **Data Access**
*   **Own Data Preparation:** Users can open Jupyter directly on the datasets they own and perform any transformations or analytics they need in preparation of using the data within the platform.
*   **Partner Data:** Users can only access partner datasets inside Jupyter if those datasets are part of a **Project workspace**.
    *   Projects ensure data is shared under explicit agreements and cannot be mixed.
    *   This protects each party’s data while still enabling collaborative analytic upon project approvals from all parties involved.
## Workspace Setup
*   When launching Jupyter, users choose a **workspace (pod size)** appropriate for their workload (e.g., Standard, Medium, Large, Extra Large).
*   The platform allocates compute resources (CPU/RAM) accordingly.
*   Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15792](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15792))

## **Analytics & Modeling**
*   Within Jupyter, users can run code for:
    *   Data preparation and transformation
    *   Statistical analysis and visualization
    *   Machine learning model development and testing
*   Common data science libraries are **pre-installed**
    *   Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15832](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15832))

* * *

##

# Configuring Jupyter Workspaces

| **Reviewer** | **Reviewed/Verified** | **Date Last Reviewed** |
| ---| ---| --- |
| ??? | ✅ / ❌ | \- |

Currently a Beta version

# Table of Contents
* * *
# Overview
When users open Jupyter Notebook on our platform, they are prompted to select a **workspace size** (pod). This determines the resources allocated to their session. Pod size availability is controlled per company via **Back Office configuration**, while the actual resource values are sourced from a central **engineering configuration table**.

By default, companies have access to **Small, Medium, and Large** pods. BackOffice staff can enable or restrict available options per company (e.g., only Small and Extra Large).
# User Flow

1. User selects **“Open Jupyter Notebook.”**
    1. From **Own Data Preparation**, or
    2. from within a **Project Workspace**
2. A configuration modal appears showing available workspace options.
    *   Example options:
        *   **Standard Workspace (Small)** – 2 CPUs, 8GB RAM
        *   **Medium Workspace** – 4 CPUs, 32GB RAM
        *   **Large Workspace** – 6 CPUs, 50GB RAM
        *   **Extra Large Workspace** – 6 CPUs, 108GB RAM
3. The user chooses the appropriate pod size and confirms.
4. Resources are allocated, and the notebook launches.

_Note: Options shown depend on the company’s Back Office configuration._

## UI Workflow
![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/1632be85-2e9a-4d1d-a446-9cbfa6a45af3/image.png)
# Back Office Flow
1. Go to **Back Office** → **Companies** → **Context Menu** → **Manage Subscriptions**.
2. On the **Jupyter Notebook Subscription**, click **Configuration**.
3. Select which pod sizes the company should have access to (default: Small, Medium, Large, Extra Large).
4. Save changes.
5. User-facing Jupyter options update automatically based on this configuration.
## UI Workflow
![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/fb6d5984-26e5-4353-996b-00bfd6239345/image.png)![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/ee5f1991-db34-4054-8286-37b1aa946fe7/image.png)![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/263c6d6c-3d5c-43e8-8b6c-3ac730456446/image.png)

* * *
# How to Update this Feature
Pod sizes and resource values are sourced from an **engineering configuration table**. Updates to this require coordination between:
1. **Integrations** – initiate/align changes.
2. **Engineering** – update the configuration table.
    1. Ensure all environments are updated consistently, unless explicitly directed to have different pod sizes per environment.
3. **Product** –
    *   Update **Intercom user-facing documentation** (link: [**How to Effectively Manage Your Jupyter Environment**](https://help.omnisient.com/en/articles/10472962-how-to-effectively-manage-your-jupyter-environment)**)**
    *   Update this internal workflow documentation.

# Overview
Selections allow users to create a sub-set of customers from their combined data based on various attributes to create a precision audience for marketing purposes. For example, creating a segment of customers that are over the age of 30 and have yet to purchase a property.

Currently the selection capability creates audiences with only one record per customer id, even if other fields are included that are at a lower granularity. The request is that when other fields are included in the selection file, that the audience is created to be unique on ALL the fields included in the selection. In other words, if a customer has 3 different values for a field called affluence segments and the affluence segment fields is included in the export file, then the file should include 3 records for this customer. This is for enrichments/extractions, not activations.

Not all project templates support the selections feature. Refer to specific project documentation for this detail here in Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15812](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15812))

* * *
# How it Works
Users make use of our selection builder tool which allows users to filter data based on attributes/columns that are found within their datasets.

For example, creating a segment of customers that are over the age of 30 and have yet to purchase a property. This may look at an "Age" column in the user's own dataset and the "Owns Property" column from their partner's dataset. By using filtering out these customers we are able to create a niche segment that users can export or activate to our supported activation channel for marketing purposes.
![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/a6376a71-22a6-46a7-ade6-2fbf755e7d7d/image.png)

## Targeting Own Customers
1. Project Detail View > Selections Widget > Make Selection
2. For "Customer Base": Choose "Own Customer"
    1. This option enables the system to know which tokens to use for a customer record. See Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16052](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16052))
3. For "Intended Use": Choose either "Activation", "Export", "Save Criteria"
    1. **Activation:**
        1. This is if the user intends on pushing the audience to a supported activation channel
    2. **Export:**
        1. This option will allow the user to download either the target or control segments. We do not allow the user to push this audience to an activation channel as it will not be in the correct format.
    3. **Save Criteria:**
        1. This option will merely save the configuration of the selection so that the user may reuse it at a later stage.
4. Setup filter criteria. See Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16012](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16012))
5. Setup additional details
    1. **Activation:**
        1. The user will provide a friendly name
        2. User is only able to define a target
    2. **Export:**
        1. The user will provide a friendly name
        2. The user can save the segment as a new table within own data preparation environment.
            1. The user will be required to provide a table name for this new table.
            2. The table is saved in the user's own data preparation space once back office approval is complete. Private ([https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16072](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-16072))
            3. The table should be available to use within the analytics tools (currently not working so TBC)
        3. The user can define a target and control size to split the segment into smaller sub-sets for A/B testing.
        4. The user is also able to select which columns to export.
        5. Only overlapped data will be exported.
        6. When selecting export, you will be presented with 2 dedupe options
            1. Deduplicate by Customer ID
            2. Return All Distinct Records
            3. This allows you to select one row count per customer or multiple row counts per customer, per article the are associated to.
    3. **Save Criteria:**
        1. The user will only provide a friendly name

## Selection Builder
The Audience Builder gives you more control, better clarity, and fast performance. Click Apply Filters once you’ve set up your conditions, and the builder will do the heavy lifting all at once.

Use the numbered guide on the image to explore each part of the Audience Builder:

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/970179ac-a637-40e6-8671-604c881c6e44/image.png)

| Number | Description |
| ---| --- |
| 1\. AND/OR logic | Use AND when all conditions must be true, and OR when any condition can be true.<br><br>Combine them to create complex, flexible filters - like “People who signed up AND made a purchase” or “Customers in Cape Town OR Johannesburg”. |
| 2\. Table Selector | Choose which dataset (or table) you want to apply your filter to. Only one table is selected per rule. |
| 3\. Column Selector | Once you've selected a table, you'll see a list of columns from that table. Choose the one you want to filter on. |
| 4. Filtering Tools | Based on the column type (text, number, or date), this dropdown will give you relevant filtering options - like “greater than” for numbers or “contains” for text. |
| 5\. Value Input | This is where you enter your filter value:<br>Numbers show a numeric input<br>Dates open a date picker<br>Text gives a text field |
| 6\. Add Rule / Add Rule Set | Add Rule lets you add another condition to your current filter set.<br>Add Rule Set creates a nested filter group - great for advanced logic like:<br>“(Age > 30 AND Gender is Female) OR (Location is Gauteng AND Purchased Product X)”.<br>This nesting is ideal for advanced queries - think of it like building layered filters in tools like Excel or Notion. |
| 7\. Action Buttons | Clear Conditions resets everything in the builder so you can start fresh.<br>Apply Filters runs your full filter logic after you’ve finished setting it up. This makes the experience faster and avoids reloading with every small change. |

## Powerful Filtering Tools
The Audience Builder offers a range of operators based on the type of column selected - whether it's text, numeric, or date data. These operators help you filter and define your audience with precision by surfacing only the relevant options for each data type.

Here’s a breakdown of all the supported operators in the Audience Builder and what they do:
### **Numeric Columns**
These include fields like age, income, number of purchases, or any other data expressed as numbers. Use these operators to filter values based on exact matches, ranges, or thresholds.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/6dc52a3a-6aa5-4337-ba12-94add89e5303/image.png)
#### Numeric Operator Breakdown

| Operator | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Equal to | Returns rows where the column value is exactly the number you specify |
| Not equal to | Excludes rows where the column value matches the number you enter. |
| Greater than | Finds values strictly higher than the number you provide. |
| Greater than or equal to | Includes values that are either equal to or higher than the number you set. |
| Less than | Returns values strictly lower than the number you enter. |
| Less than or equal to | Includes values that are equal to or less than your specified number. |
| Between | Filters for values that fall within a number range you define (inclusive of both ends). |
| Not Between | Excludes any values that fall within the number range you specify. |
| Number In | Allows you to select multiple exact numbers from a mulit-select dropdown, returns any rows matching one of them. |

### **Text Columns**
These cover fields that contain words, names, categories, or descriptions. Text operators help you search for specific keywords or match exact text values across multiple options.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/b5223828-d1ec-4abe-b73d-96052076ac40/image.png)
#### Text Operator Breakdown

| Operator | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Text contains | Looks for rows where the column contains the word or phrase you add. |
| Text does not contain | Excludes rows where the column includes the word or phrase. |
| Text is exactly | Matches only rows that are an exact match (case-sensitive) to the text you enter. |
| Text in | Lets you select multiple exact text values from a mulit-select dropdown - returns rows that match any of them. |

### **Date Columns**
These are fields that store time-related data like sign-up dates, purchase dates, or last activity timestamps. Date operators let you target specific days, or ranges like "before" or "after" a certain date.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/aaa9f442-7a63-4f61-8b38-8fb31a631b5f/image.png)
#### Date Operator Breakdown

| Operator | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Date is | Returns rows that match a specific date exactly. |
| Date is on or before | Includes all rows on or before the selected date. |
| Date is on or after | Includes all rows on or after the selected date. |
| Date is between | Filters for rows where the date falls within a range you choose (inclusive). |
| Date is not between | Excludes rows where the date falls within the selected date range. |

# Meta

Official Meta Documentation [here](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2082575038703844?id=2469097953376494)

## Data Requirements
### **Customer List**

Lists should be:
*   be either CSV or TXT files.
*   include at least 100 customers.
*   include at least one main identifier.
*   use the correct column formatting that matches each identifier type.
## Formatting Guidelines
### **Main Identifiers**

We currently only match on Email Address and Phone Number

| **Identifier** | **Column header** | **Formatting guidelines** | **Examples** |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| Email address | email | We accept email addresses in up to three separate columns. Only one email address can go in each cell. All universal email address formats are accepted. | <br>Emily@mail.com<br>John@mail.com<br>Helen@mail.com<br> |
| Phone number | phone | Phone numbers must include a country code to be used for matching, even if they're all from the same country. For example, a one must precede a phone number in the United States. We accept phone numbers in up to three separate columns, with or without punctuation.<br>**Note:** Make sure that you include the country code as part of your customers' phone numbers, even if all of your data is from the same country. | <br><br><br><br> |
| Mobile advertiser ID | madid | We accept two types of mobile advertiser IDs: Android's advertising ID (AAID), which Google provides as part of Android advertising and Apple's advertising identifier (IDFA), which Apple provides as part of iOS in its ads framework. | <br><br> |
| Facebook app user ID | appuid | An ID corresponding to someone who uses an app that can be retrieved through the Facebook SDK. We accept numerical user IDs associated with your Facebook application. | <br><br><br> |
| Facebook Page user ID | pageuid | An ID corresponding to someone who has interacted with your business' Facebook Page. This does not refer to a user's personal Facebook profile page. We accept numerical user IDs associated with your business' Facebook Page. | <br><br><br> |

### **Additional Identifiers** (Optional)
We recommend using these identifiers along with at least one main identifier to increase the chances of getting a better match rate.

We do not use any of these to match on, but would be good to keep in mind to expand our offering in the future

| **Identifier** | **Column header** | **Formatting guidelines** | **Examples** |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| First name | fn | We accept first name and first name initial, with or without accents. Initials can be provided with or without a full stop.<br> | <br><br><br> |
| Surname | ln | We accept full last names with or without accents. | <br><br><br> |
| City | ct | We accept full names of towns and cities. | <br><br><br> |
| County/Region | st | We accept full names of US and international states and provinces, as well as the abbreviated versions of US states. | <br><br><br> |
| Country<br> | country | Countries must be provided as an [ISO two-letter country code](https://l.facebook.com/l.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fen.wikipedia.org%2Fwiki%2FISO_3166-1_alpha-2&h=AT1bEJ-Tt8jMxFYifMKy6-0tS0Z-Yatewvscl9BFH13Jh3ZXpX4saVj7hHhOOevHCH3Yuyufmiliw8rFhNc0docNavrvIxB7sBxSYQ4pDJpj2pF-jFHKQ-DR0RgCKcsd3mq-TC1DSLSo-foXxxSOq_IEX_0), even if they're all from the same country. Because we match on a global scale, this simple step helps us match as many people as possible from your list.<br> | <br><br><br> |
| Zip/postcode<br> | zip | We accept US and international ZIP and postcodes. US ZIP codes may include a 4-digit extension as long as they are separated by a hyphen. The extension is not required and will not further improve match rate. | <br><br><br> |
| Date of birth<br> | dob | We accept 18 different date formats to accommodate a range of month, day and year combinations, with or without punctuation. | <br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br> |
| Year of birth<br> | doby | We accept year of birth as a 4-digit number, YYYY. | <br><br><br> |
| Gender<br> | gen | We accept gender in the form of an initial, such as 'F' for female and 'M' for male. | <br><br> |
| Age<br> | age | We accept age as a numerical value. | <br><br><br> |

### **Data Processing Options** (Optional)

We do not use this as yet, but would be good to keep in mind

| **Identifier type** | **Column header** | **Description and formatting guidelines** | **Examples** |
| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| Data Processing Options | data\_processing\_options | Use "LDU" to enable [Limited Data Use](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1151133471911882) for California based customers. Use no value for customers who haven't asked you to limit their data use.<br>**How to use this column:** Use it to tell Meta to limit the data use of a customer in California. | <br> |
| Data processing options - state | data\_processing\_options\_state | Use "1,000" for customers in California. Use "0" or no value for customers who aren't in California (or if you don't know where they are). Our system will check their location.<br>**How to use this column:** Use it to tell Meta if a customer is in California. | <br><br> |
| Data processing options - country | data\_processing\_options\_country | Use "1" for customers in the United States. Use "0" or no value for customers outside of the US (or if you don't know where they are). Our system will check their location.<br>**How to use this column:** Use it to tell us if a customer is in the United States. | <br><br> |

Once the audience has been registered the audience will be accessible via the Marketplace screens for any company that has access to the "Audiences" subscription.

### RACI Matrix
*   **R (Responsible):** Person(s) doing the work.
*   **A (Accountable):** Person who owns the task’s success and signs off.
*   **C (Consulted):** Person(s) providing input, advice, or expertise.
*   **I (Informed):** Person(s) kept in the loop on progress.

| **Task** | **Requester** | **Data Science** | **Engineering** | **Product** | **Back Office (MENA)** |
| ---| ---| ---| ---| ---| --- |
| **Submit Request** | R | I | I | I | I |
| **Ensure Source Data in Correct Format for Activation** | R/A | C | C | I | I |
| **Validate Audience Segment** | I | R/A | I | I | I |
| **Create Segment Table** | I | R/A | I | I | I |
| **Register Dataset on Front-End** | I | R/A | C | I | I |
| **Request Execution** | I | R/A | C | I | I |
| **Call API & Pipeline Execution** | I | I | R/A | I | I |
| **Verify Marketplace Availability** | A | I | R | C | I |

### Steps
![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/42665c43-f0e6-4e87-ab7c-6676a37b51e4/image.png)
1. **Audience Request Initiated** **(Requested via email thread 📥)**
    1. Responsible: Omnisient MENA
    2. MENA team contacts Data Science (Donovan or Nisarg) with:
        1. Desired Audience Segment(s)
            1. name (will be the one displayed on the UI)
            2. description
            3. cost
            4. icon (any filled, rounded icon from this list [https://fonts.google.com/icons?icon.style=Rounded](https://fonts.google.com/icons?icon.style=Rounded) - [@Tegan Carton-Barber](#user_mention#87829007) can assist with this choice)
2. **Data Science Validates**
    1. Responsible: Data Science
    2. Confirms if segment logic and data already exist. (This should be the case as this flow assumes that the audience segments have already been created from a data perspective - see [technical segment setup](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-15452?block=block-9789303b-1cb2-4074-8852-a6e8c1955ab6) documentation)
3. **Create Segment Table** **(Send update to email thread 📥)**
    1. Responsible: Data Science

4. **Engineering to Call API**
    1. Responsible: Engineering

        1. match field (statically chosen and is set to be both email and phone numbers - note that phone numbers need to be in a specific format)
5. **Ensure that the audience segment is available on the Marketplace UI**
    1. Responsible: Engineering

# Overview
The subscriptions feature allows a back office user the ability to assign certain project templates or features to a specific company for a defined time period. Subscriptions are usually governed by contractual agreements outside of the platform.

* * *

# Table of Contents
* * *
# Overview
Back Office Approval is required for all audiences that are being activated to any of our supported activation channels. These requests stem from Marketplace as well as our Selections from within projects.

* * *
# Workflow
1. Navigate to Back Office → Audience Approvals
2. Find the audience that is pending approval in the list, it should have the status Requires Review
3. Click the "Review" button
4. Ensure the contents of the request are correct for the client based on contracts in place.
    1. Ensure the user is allowed to send this audience segment to the selected activation channel
    2. Ensure the activation channel is correct
    3. Ensure the Ad Account number is correct (if possible)
    4. Check audience size
    5. Check expiry date
5. You can:
    1. Approve → This will upload the audience to the Omnisient Ad Account and share the audience to the selected activation channel
    2. Reject → Will go into a "Rejected" state. The client will not be able to continue and will have to resubmit if a mistake was made.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/25a1abb3-1dbe-427b-9b0f-3d65568f2875/image.png)
![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/8694f810-2d03-440d-a185-13930e48858a/image.png)

Approvals from Back Office, whilst acting as a failsafe, places a lot of risk on Omnisient. It is crucial to ensure that when accepting or rejecting approvals you are certain. It is beneficial to check in with Account Management in the Production environment.

* * *
# Features

| **Feature** | **Notes** |
| ---| --- |
| View Audience Details | Submitted By, Data Sources, Uploaded By, Activation Channel, Ad Account, Match Fields, Selection Details, Pre-Built Audience Info (if applicable), Expiry Date (only for Pre-Built Audiences currently) |
| Approve | This will upload the audience to the Omnisient Ad Account and share the audience to the selected activation channel |
| Reject | The client will not be able to continue and will have to resubmit if a mistake was made. |

3. Actioned by Back Office User
4. Removed from List (Either approved or deleted)

The Datasets section is where you view and manage all datasets available to your organization. This includes datasets you’ve uploaded and registered, datasets shared with you by connection partners, and tools that allow you to prepare, transform, and generate derived datasets for use in projects.
## My Datasets
The My Datasets tab displays all datasets uploaded by your organization. Datasets are grouped based on their current processing, registration, and sharing status.

| Unregistered[](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/v/dc/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-46312)<br> | This table acts as the dataset lobby. Newly uploaded datasets appear here while they are being processed. You can review potential issues, such as high error rates or possible PII leaks, to ensure the dataset is in optimal condition before registration.<br><br>At this stage, datasets can also be mapped. Mapping is a crucial step to ensure the dataset is fit for its intended purpose. The mapping process confirms that all required columns and information are available for use in future projects. |
| ---| --- |
| Registered<br>[](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/v/dc/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-46332)<br> | These datasets have completed processing and registration and are ready to be used in projects. Available datasets can also be shared with connection partners. Deleting a dataset will trigger a confirmation modal if it is currently shared. This helps prevent accidentally removing a source dataset that one or more connection partners may be using.<br><br>These datasets can also be mapped. Mapping is a crucial step to ensure the dataset is fit for its intended purpose. It confirms that all required columns and information are available for use when the dataset is included in a project. |
| Dataset Share | This table lists registered datasets that have been shared with connection partners. You can manage or revoke partner access to a dataset at any time from here. |

### **Dataset Types**
Dataset types help categorize datasets based on their purpose and the kind of data they contain. These types are used throughout the platform to guide processing and downstream usage.

| Dataset Type | Description | Mapping Supported |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Custom / Derived | A dataset created on the platform using tools such as SQLPad, then registered for use in the platform. |  |
| Customer | A dataset containing customer information, including PII that must be anonymized. |  |
| Customer (Activation) | Contains single hash values intended for upload to activation channels such as Meta and TikTok. |  |
| Dimension | Descriptive dataset information that does not contain PII and does not require anonymization. |  |
| [](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/v/dc/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-46292)<br>Transaction | Transactional data where each row represents an individual transaction at a point in time. Does not contain PII and does not require anonymization. | ✅ |
| Other | A dataset containing mixed information that may include PII and may require anonymization. |  |

## Partner Datasets
This tab shows datasets that have been shared with your organization by connection partners. From here, you can review incoming dataset shares and decide whether to accept or decline access.

| Status | Description |
| ---| --- |
| New | Requires action from you. You can either Accept or Decline the dataset share. |
| Accepted | You have accepted the dataset share. The dataset can now be used when creating a new project and will surface in the partner referencing dropdown. |
| Declined | You declined the dataset share. The dataset will not be available for use in projects. |
| Locked | The dataset share has expired. Any projects using this dataset will also become locked. |

## **Own Data Preparation**
This tab provides tools to explore, transform, and prepare your datasets for use in projects. You can also create and save new datasets, which will appear as Custom / Derived datasets under _My Datasets_.
### **Supported Tools**
The following tools are available:

| Tool | Description |
| ---| --- |
| SQLPad | Use SQLPad to write and run SQL queries to explore and prepare your data for projects. In supported projects, SQLPad can also be used to generate exports, allowing you to extract query results for external use through the platform’s export approval process.<br>​<br>👉 [How to Create a SQLPad Export](https://help.omnisient.com/en/articles/13229825-step-by-step-guide-how-to-create-a-sqlpad-export)<br>👉 [Approving SQLPad Exports Created On Your Data](https://help.omnisient.com/en/articles/13212744-step-by-step-guide-approving-sqlpad-exports-created-on-your-data)<br>​<br>👉 [How to Assess SQLPad Exports with Confidence](https://help.omnisient.com/en/articles/13230382-up-skilling-guide-how-to-assess-sqlpad-exports-with-confidence) |
| Jupyter Notebook | Create code and data visualizations and effortlessly enhance your data preparation. |
| Dataset Mapper | Prepare your dataset by mapping its columns to the required fields. |

##  Status Overview

# Unregistered Datasets

Unregistered datasets are newly uploaded datasets that have not yet been finalized or made available for use in projects. At this stage, the dataset is still undergoing review and validation to ensure it meets the required quality and compliance standards before being registered.

During the unregistered stage, you can:
*   Review dataset metadata and processing results
*   Identify potential issues such as high error rates, duplicate values, or possible PII exposure
*   Validate that the dataset contains the necessary fields for its intended use
*   Configure dataset fields and identifiers to support future uploads and matching

Unregistered datasets act as a staging step, allowing teams to confirm that the dataset is complete, accurate, and properly structured before it becomes an official registered dataset in the system.
### Statuses

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Under Review | The dataset is undergoing internal review |
| Requires Review | The dataset requires user review. It has either been flagged for a PII leak or a high error rate |
| Queued For Preparation | PII checks and awaiting the hydration queue |
| Data Prep Queued | Queued for hydration |
| Data Prep in Progress | Hydration is currently in progress |
| Data Prep Failed | Hydration has failed |
| Ready | Hydration completed successfully and the dataset is ready for registration |
| Failed | ? |

### Dataset Actions

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/884109d5-47a3-488c-8573-99fd36ce2308/image.png)

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Delete | The dataset will be deleted |
| [Map Dataset](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-48972) | Allows you to map the chosen dataset to a specified dataset type |
| Register | Register the dataset in order to use it in projects or share it with connection partners |
| Review | The dataset needs to be reviewed as there were either PII leak issues or high error rate issues that need to be actioned by either deleting the dataset or marking it as safe |

## Unregistered Dataset Detail View
The **Dataset Detail View** provides a deeper look into an individual unregistered dataset and allows for configuration before registration.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/f3620485-7f4b-42e2-af2e-4652310f5a0b/image.png)
### 1\. Editable Dataset Settings
You can make the following updates before registration:
*   **Edit Dataset Display Name**
*   **Change Dataset Type**

### 2\. Dataset Summary
At the top of the detail view, you can see key metadata about the dataset:

| Field | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Dataset Owner | The user who uploaded the dataset |
| Row Count | Total number of rows in the dataset |
| Unique Personal Identifiers | A list of unique identifiers detected |
| Activation Compatible | Indicates whether the dataset was flagged as compatible for activation |

### 3\. Dataset Quality Widget
This widget provides visibility into the overall quality of the dataset. This helps identify data quality issues early, before the dataset is registered or used.
**What you can see:**
*   Columns with **high duplication rates**
*   Columns with **high error rates**
**Views available:**
*   **Bar chart** for a visual overview
*   **Table view** showing detailed metrics, including uploaded PII fields

### 4\. Dataset Sample Widget
Displays a preview sample of the dataset, showing the different columns and example values.
*   Columns marked as **PII** are masked and displayed as `*secure*`
*   Allows for a quick sanity check of column structure and data format
####   

### Dataset Fields Widget
This widget lists **all fields (columns)** contained within the dataset and is where most field-level configuration happens.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/51ed7ff3-5aa3-4b88-99ba-c7b6e1ce1ccf/image.png)

**For each field, you can view:**
*   Column name
*   Description
*   Whether the field is marked as **PII**
*   Whether it is marked as:
    *   **Unique ID**
    *   **Dedupe ID**

#### Editable Field Attributes
You can edit fields to:
*   **Add or update a description**
*   **Select a Unique Key**
    *   A key from the client’s internal systems that uniquely identifies a customer
    *   _This is not considered PII_
*   **Assign Dedupe Identifiers for future uploads**
    *   Optional fields used to determine whether an incoming record should **replace an existing record** with the same value
    *   More than one field can be selected as a dedupe identifier

# Available Dataset

## Overview
**Available datasets** are datasets that have completed processing and have been successfully registered in the platform. Once registered, datasets are ready to be used in projects and can also be shared with approved connection partners.

Available datasets represent a stable, project-ready version of your data. They support ongoing use cases such as collaboration and project creation.
### Key Capabilities
Available datasets allow you to:
*   Use datasets directly in **projects**
*   Share datasets with **connection partners**
*   Map and configure fields to ensure project compatibility
*   Upload new versions of a dataset while maintaining historical tracking
### Statuses

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Processing | Dataset is in the process of being registered |
| Ready | Dataset is ready to be shared or used in a project |
| Failed | Processing has failed, this could be due to the chosen customer identifier |
| Marked for Delete | The dataset has been flagged for deletion, it will be deleted during the next deletion cycle |

### Dataset Actions

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Delete | The dataset will be deleted, a confirmation modal will show if the dataset is currently involved in a share. This helps prevent accidentally removing a source dataset that one or more connection partners may be using. |
| [Map Dataset](https://app.clickup.com/9012824942/docs/8ck9jve-21812/8ck9jve-48972) | Allows you to map the chosen dataset to a specified dataset type |
| Share | Share this dataset with a specified connection partner |
| Update | Update the dataset with a new customer identifier, this will set the dataset back into a processing state in order to process the dataset with the new customer identifier |

## Available Dataset Detail View
The **Available Dataset Detail View** provides a complete overview of the dataset, including metadata, project usage, collaboration settings, upload history, and lineage information.

![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/5db76856-1b7f-464f-8eab-689ff86a053f/image.png)
### 1\. Editable Dataset Settings
You can make the following updates before a dataset share:

| Field | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Dataset Owner | The user who uploaded the dataset |
| Row Count | Total number of rows in the dataset |
| Customer Identifier | The identifier used when the dataset was registered. If needed, the Customer Identifier can be updated using the Retry action. |

### 2\. Dataset Summary
Within the detail view, you can update the dataset configuration:
*   **Edit Dataset Display Name**
*   **Change Dataset Type**
*   **Add or update Dataset Description**
### 3\. Dataset Collaboration
The **Dataset Collaboration** section shows which connection partners have access to the dataset. This widget provides a quick way to audit who the dataset is shared with and for how long.

This includes:
*   A list of partners with **read access**
*   When the dataset was shared
*   When the share is set to expire
### 4\. Project Reference Widget
This widget allows you to view which projects the dataset is currently being used in.
Key behavior:
*   Only **Active** and **Locked** projects are displayed
*   Projects you do not have access to are hidden
*   Includes a quick link to navigate directly to the project
### ![](https://t9012824942.p.clickup-attachments.com/t9012824942/ed924a6f-6400-41d9-9e0a-ad1d596a0dda/image.png)

### 5\. Manage Dataset History
The **Dataset History** widget allows you to review and manage dataset uploads over time.

When new data is uploaded to an existing available dataset:
*   The new upload appears here
*   Uploads queue in this section for review and validation
*   You can investigate uploads and take action where needed
### 6\. Dataset Sample
Displays a sample preview of the dataset and its columns.
*   Fields marked as **PII** will appear as `*secure*`
*   Useful for validating formatting and column structure at a glance
### 7\. Dataset Lineage
The **Dataset Lineage** section provides deeper insight into the dataset’s structure and quality. It contains information similar to the unregistered dataset view, including dataset quality and dataset fields.
#### Dataset Quality
Gain insight into dataset health by reviewing:
*   Columns with **high duplication**
*   Columns with **high error rates**
Quality can be viewed as:
*   A **bar chart** (visual overview)
*   A **table** (detailed breakdown, including uploaded PII)
#### Dataset Fields
View all fields contained in the dataset, including:
*   Column names
*   Descriptions
*   Whether a field is marked as **PII**
*   Whether it is set as:
    *   **Unique ID**
    *   **Dedupe ID**
### 8\. Non-PII Dataset Fields
This widget provides a view of all **non-PII fields** contained within the dataset.

You can also:
*   Add or update or add a description for each non-PII field

# Table of Contents

* * *
# Overview
This is a popup that governs how a dataset is shared to a partner. It is important that all of our downstream processes and workflows take this agreement into account.

# Agreement Fields
## Partner
Which partner/company the dataset is shared with 💡Ensure you have a connection with this company
## Access Duration
*       *   Defines the duration that the partner will have access to the datset
    *   Once this expiry date is reached, the dataset will expire for the partner and any outputs the partner has created using this dataset will expire/lock.
    *   ⚠️ Currently activated audiences from selections are not unshared/removed from Activation channels upon expiry.
## Usage terms
## Visible Data
*       *   All Data in Overlap - The partner will see/access all data even if it doesn't match records in their own data
    *   Only Matching Data - The partner will only see/access data that matches records in their own data
## Analysis Fields
This defines what fields will be visible to the partner
## Partner Selections
*       *   Disallow selections
        *   Selections widget should not be displayed and partner may not make selections on this data
*       *   Allow selections
        *   Selections widget is displayed and partner may make selections on this data
        *   Owner/Sharer may select which fields can be used to select on. All downstream logic/gates should respect by this.
## Filter Data (TBC if inclusive or exclusive or what is shared by default???)
This allows the owner/sharer the ability to remove certain rows from the data by creating a sub-selection of the data. For example, not allow the partner to access customer that are over the age of 30. This sub-selection of data is what is shared with the partner. All downstream logic/gates should respect by this.

# Dataset Shares

## Summary
Registered datasets that have been shared with connection partners. Access can be reviewed or revoked at any time.
## Statues

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| New | The dataset share is awaiting approval from the connection partner |
| Accepted | The connection partner has approved the share |
| Declined | The connection partner has declined the share |
| Deactivated | The share has been deactivated, it can be reactivated |
| Locked | The dataset share has passed its expiry date |

## Table Actions

| Name | Description |
| ---| --- |
| Deactivate | The dataset share will be deactivated, all the projects the connection partner is using it in will be locked |
| Edit | Edit the dataset share configuration |
| Reactivate | Reactivate the dataset share, all the projects a connection partner is using this dataset in will be unlocked |

# Transaction Dataset

## About this Dataset Type
A transactional dataset is designed to capture individual transactions or events, such as sales activity. Each row in the dataset represents a single transaction at a specific point in time, making this dataset type ideal for tracking behaviour, performance, and trends over time.

Transactional datasets typically contain non-sensitive transaction details and do not include personally identifiable information (PII), meaning they do not require anonymisation. Where linking is required, transactions may include a consistent identifier (such as a loyalty or customer ID) that allows activity to be associated with a customer record without exposing personal details.

Data pertaining to transactions that can be summed together using various dimensions, with date, value and other info regarding the transaction. Can also be pre-aggregated to specific dimensions before uploading.
### When it's used
TBC
### Where it's used
TBC

| Project Type | Why |
| ---| --- |
|  |  |
|  |  |

### Required fields

| Field name | Data type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Transaction Date | Datetime | The date and time when the transaction occurred. |
| Sales Value | Decimal | The total monetary value of the transaction. |

### Additional fields
These fields aren’t required, but we recommend mapping them to get the most value from your dataset.

| Field name | Data type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Transaction Identifier | String | A unique identifier for the transaction. |
| Year | Integer | The year in which the transaction occurred. |
| Month | Integer | The month in which the transaction occurred. |
| Day | Integer | The day of the month on which the transaction occurred. |
| Time | Datetime | The time at which the transaction occurred. |
| Highest-level Product Code | String | The code representing the highest level in the product hierarchy. |
| Highest-level Product Description | String | The description of the highest-level product category. |
| Middle-level Product Code | String | The code representing the middle level in the product hierarchy. |
| Middle-level Product Description | String | The description of the middle-level product category. |
| Lowest-level Product Code | String | The code representing the most granular product level. |
| Lowest-level Product Description | String | The description of the most granular product level. |
| Site Code | String | A unique code identifying the site or location where the transaction occurred. |
| Site Name | String | The name of the site or location. |
| Site Type | String | The type of site (for example, store, online, or warehouse). |
| Site Description | String | Additional descriptive information about the site. |
| Discount Value | Decimal | The monetary value of any discount applied to the transaction. |
| Promotion Code | String | The code associated with a promotion applied to the transaction. |
| Promotion Flag | Boolean | Indicates whether a promotion was applied to the transaction. |
| Payment Type Code | String | A code identifying the payment method used. |
| Payment Type Description | String | A descriptive label for the payment method used. |

# Customer Dataset

## About this Dataset Type
This is a dataset which contains information about your customer and contains PII that needs to be anonymized.

The Customer Dataset contains core demographic, geographic, and segmentation attributes used to uniquely identify and profile customers. It serves as the foundational reference dataset for customer-level analytics, matching, enrichment, and segmentation use cases.

Customer master or CRM data containing a single record per cusomer with PII and other customer attributes like demographics.
### **Purpose**
*   Provides a unique customer identifier for cross-dataset joins
*   Enables demographic and geographic segmentation
*   Supports behavioral profiling and value-based classification
*   Serves as the anchor dataset for linking transactional, account, policy, and product interactions

One record per **unique customer**.

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Joining Date | Datetime | The date and time when the customer first registered, subscribed, or became active. Used for cohort analysis and lifecycle tracking. |
| Customer Type | String | Classification of the customer (e.g., individual, business, premium, loyalty member). |
| Birth Year | Date (YYYY) | The customer’s year of birth. Used for age segmentation and demographic analysis. |
| Gender | String | The customer’s gender as provided or inferred. |
| City | String | The city where the customer resides. |
| Province or State | String | The province, region, or state where the customer resides. |
| Country | String | The country of residence. |
| Customer Lifestyles | String | Lifestyle segment or behavioral classification (e.g., health-conscious, frequent traveler, tech-savvy). |
| Customer Affluence | String | Indicator of purchasing power or income segment (e.g., low, middle, high affluence). |
| Customer Value | String | Internal value classification based on spend, engagement, or profitability (e.g., high-value, medium-value, low-value). |
| Customer Preference | String | Key preferences or interests associated with the customer (e.g., product category affinity). |

| Other Descriptive Attribute 4 | String | Additional optional attribute used for extended customer profiling. |
| Other Descriptive Attribute 5 | String | Additional optional attribute used for extended customer profiling. |

# Product Dataset

## About this Dataset Type
The Product Dataset defines the hierarchical structure, classification, and attributes of products. It enables product-level analytics, category rollups, brand analysis, and product segmentation across multiple hierarchy levels.

Data containing information on products, that will be used to link with a transactional table using a key or code.
### **Purpose**
*   Provides a unique lowest-level product identifier (e.g., SKU)
*   Supports multi-level category aggregation (lowest to highest hierarchy)
*   Enables brand-level and classification analysis
*   Allows binary flag segmentation (e.g., premium, private label, essential items)

One record per **lowest-level product (SKU)**.

### Additional fields
These fields aren’t required, but we recommend mapping them to get the most value from your dataset.

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Lowest Level Product Description | String | Description of the product at the most detailed level (e.g., full SKU description including size/variant). |
| 2nd Level Product Code | String | Identifier for the second level in the product hierarchy (e.g., sub-category). |
| 2nd Level Product Description | String | Description corresponding to the second-level product classification. |
| 3rd Level Product Code | String | Identifier for the third level in the product hierarchy (e.g., category level). |
| 3rd Level Product Description | String | Description corresponding to the third-level product classification. |
| Highest Level Product Code / Identifier | String | Identifier for the top-level product grouping (e.g., department or division). |
| Highest Level Product Description | String | Description of the highest-level product grouping. |
| Product Brand Code | String | Unique identifier representing the product’s brand. |
| Product Brand Description | String | The brand name or brand description associated with the product. |
| Barcode | String | Standard product barcode (e.g., EAN/UPC) used for scanning and retail identification. |
| Unit of Measure | String | The unit in which the product is measured or sold (e.g., kg, litre, pack, unit). |
| Own Label Binary Flag | String | Indicator showing whether the product is an own-label item (e.g., 1 = Yes, 0 = No). |
| Private Label Binary Flag | String | Indicator showing whether the product is classified as private label (e.g., 1 = Yes, 0 = No). |
| Premium Product Binary Code | String | Indicator showing whether the product is categorized as premium (e.g., 1 = Yes, 0 = No). |
| Essential Item Binary Flag | String | Indicator showing whether the product is classified as an essential item (e.g., 1 = Yes, 0 = No). |
| Other Product Binary Flag 1 | String | Additional configurable binary flag for custom product classification. |
| Other Product Binary Flag 2 | String | Additional configurable binary flag for custom product classification. |

# Location Dataset

## About this Dataset Type
The Location Dataset contains metadata about physical and/or online sites where transactions or interactions occur. It supports geographic analysis, operational segmentation, and channel-based reporting.

Information relating to each site's or location's decriptive infomation - NOT relating to customer address, this should be part of customer table.
Should be join-able to a transaction type table using a unique site key.
### **Purpose**
*   Provides a unique site identifier
*   Enables geographic segmentation (country, state, city)
*   Supports format and site-type analysis
*   Allows geospatial analysis via latitude and longitude
*   Differentiates online vs physical presence

One record per **unique site/location**.

|  |  |
|  |  |

| ---| ---| --- |

### Additional fields
These fields aren’t required, but we recommend mapping them to get the most value from your dataset.

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Site Name | String | The official name of the site or location (e.g., store name, branch name, distribution center name). |
| Site Type | String | Classification of the site (e.g., retail store, warehouse, online store, head office). |
| Site Format | String | Format category of the site (e.g., flagship, express, mall-based, standalone). |
| Site Description | String | Additional descriptive details about the site, including characteristics or operational notes. |
| Online Binary Flag | String | Indicator showing whether the site operates online (e.g., 1 = Yes, 0 = No). |
| Site Country | String | The country where the site is located. |

| Site City | String | The city where the site is located. |

| Site LON | Decimal | Longitude coordinate of the site location. Should allow sufficient precision (e.g., up to 6+ decimal places) to support accurate geolocation. |

# Account Balance Dataset

## About this Dataset Type
The Account Balance Dataset captures time-based financial balance snapshots for customer accounts. It supports financial analytics, time-series reporting, and account-level performance monitoring.

Repeated snapshots of accounts with information on balance as at that point in time, the data is not summable across snapshots.
### **Purpose**
*   Links customers to one or more accounts
*   Enables point-in-time balance reporting
*   Supports time-based aggregation (year, month, day, time)
*   Allows account-type segmentation and status monitoring
*   Facilitates financial trend and exposure analysis

One record per **account per balance timestamp**.
### When it's used
TBC
### Where it's used
TBC

| Project Type | Why |
| ---| --- |
|  |  |
|  |  |

### Required fields

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Customer Reference Key / Customer Identifier | String | Unique identifier linking the balance record to a specific customer. Must align with the Customer dataset identifier for accurate joins. |
| Account Reference Key / Account Identifier | String | Unique identifier for the account associated with the balance record. Used to distinguish between multiple accounts held by the same customer. |

### Additional fields
These fields aren’t required, but we recommend mapping them to get the most value from your dataset.

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---| ---| --- |
| Balance Date and Time | Datetime | The exact date and time when the account balance was recorded. Used for time-based analysis and reporting. |
| Year | Integer | The calendar year extracted from the balance date for partitioning and aggregation purposes. |
| Month | Integer | The calendar month extracted from the balance date (1–12) for reporting and grouping. |
| Day | Integer | The calendar day extracted from the balance date (1–31). |
| Time | Timeonly | The time component of the balance record, captured separately where required for intraday analysis. |
| Balance | Decimal | The account balance amount at the specified date and time. Should support appropriate precision for financial values. |
| Account Type Code | String | Encoded classification of the account type (e.g., savings, credit, transactional). |
| Account Type Description | String | Human-readable description corresponding to the account type code. |
| Account Status | String | Current status of the account at the time of the balance record (e.g., active, closed, suspended). |

*   Supports time-based reporting and snapshot analysis
*   Allows policy-type classification and status monitoring
